tables.context_before:
Monitoring/evaluation
Monitoring and evaluation should focus on early identification and timely intervention for patients
experiencing disease deterioration, as this is a common feature of bronchiectasis. Regular clinical
assessment, symptom tracking and objective investigations should be prioritised to detect worsening
conditions and guide appropriate treatment. Key aspects of monitoring include evaluating exacerbation
frequency, response to treatment, microbiology, respiratory function decline and increased need for oxygen
or ventilatory support.
header_row: R A P I D I

• History and physical examination • Adherence to airway clearance and/or pharmacological treatment • Newly developed or worsening comorbidity • The presence of new or evolving treatable traits • A review of airway clearance by an experienced respiratory physiotherapist • A high-resolution computed tomography scan of the chest • Sputum culture for bacteria, fungi and mycobacteria • Bronchoscopy if sputum cannot be obtained or culture results are inconclusive • Tests to reassess underlying causes such as allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis • A full pulmonary function assessment • Antibiotic treatment for infection • Eradication therapy for Pseudomonas aeruginosa where appropriate • Targeted treatment for non-tuberculous mycobacteria or fungal lung infections • Disease-specific therapy for newly diagnosed causes of bronchiectasis • Updated strategies for airway clearance and exercise tolerance • New long-term maintenance treatments (e.g. inhaled antibiotics, macrolides) when indicated by the present guidelines • Malnutrition: referral to a dietician; supplemental feeding • Haemoptysis: bronchial artery embolisation or surgical resection in selected cases, following multidisciplinary discussion with a thoracic surgeon experienced in bronchiectasis • Persistent or high-burden infections unresponsive to antibiotics: detailed imaging • Respiratory failure: supplemental oxygen; non-invasive ventilation; referral for lung transplantation • Recognise the deteriorating patient# • Refer to or consult with a bronchiectasis specialist Recognise and refer Assess Perform Initiate Deal with complications
